cases.input: How is the writing part of the language exam structured?

key_facts.fact: The writing part consists of three texts: one short informal text, one short formal text and one longer opinion text.
The writing part takes 55 minutes in total.
The informal and the formal text are each 50-80 words long.
The opinion text is 100-150 words long, ideally about 120 words.
The formal text type covers text types 3, 5, 6 and 7.

cases.expected_behavior: Describes the structure of the writing part using the course material.

cases.input: What are the parts of the speaking test, and how much time is there for each part?

key_facts.fact: The speaking test parts are Berätta, Dialog, Reagera (Situationer) and Din åsikt.
Berätta: 1 minute preparation and 1 minute speaking.
Dialog (1 or 2 dialogues): 30 seconds to read the instructions and 10-25 seconds per answer.
Reagera: 4-5 situations with about 20 seconds preparation and about 20 seconds speaking.
Din åsikt: choose between A and B, 1 minute preparation and 1 minute 30 seconds speaking.
The speaking test takes about 25 minutes in total.

cases.essential_rule: KF1-KF5 are all essential because the question explicitly asks for every part and the time for each part.
cases.expected_behavior: Names all speaking-test parts and gives the time for each part from the course material.

cases.input: How should I structure an argumentative opinion text (text type 4)?

key_facts.fact: Start with an introduction that states your opinion (for example with phrases such as 'Enligt mig' or 'Min åsikt är').
The body contains either two arguments on the same side, or one argument for and one against (for example 'Å ena sidan / Å andra sidan').
Use linking words such as 'För det första', 'Dessutom' and 'Sist men inte minst'.
Support the arguments with examples or reasons.
End with a conclusion or summary (for example 'Sammanfattningsvis' or 'För att sammanfatta').

cases.essential_rule: KF1, KF2 and KF5 (introduction, body, conclusion) are essential because the question asks for the structure.
cases.expected_behavior: Explains the introduction-body-conclusion structure of the opinion text from the course material.

cases.input: What should an informal message to a friend include?

key_facts.fact: An informal greeting and an informal ending.
Ask the person how they are.
React to the prompt.
Set the stage by adding background information.
Ask informal questions and give suggestions, for example to meet.

cases.expected_behavior: Lists what an informal message should include according to the course material.

cases.input: What steps should I follow when writing a complaint?

key_facts.fact: Be polite.
Say why you are writing.
Explain what is wrong, giving examples or facts.
Say what you want done.
Optionally give a deadline or contact information.
End politely.

cases.expected_behavior: Gives the complaint-writing steps from the course material.

cases.input: Why did the reviewer give Hotell Mörker a negative review?

key_facts.fact: What the hotel's website said did not match reality.
The rooms were not clean (dusty, dirty, bed linen not fresh).
The staff were not friendly or helpful and answered impolitely.
The included breakfast was poor, with little choice and food that looked old.
The hotel was far from the city and the places the reviewer wanted to visit.
The reviewer does not recommend the hotel and will not stay there again.

cases.expected_behavior: Summarises the reasons given in the negative example review.

cases.input: In the apartment advertisement, what does the rent include, and what is required of the tenant?

key_facts.fact: The rent includes heating and water.
Electricity and broadband are paid separately.
The landlord wants a reliable tenant who takes care of the apartment and respects the neighbours.
No pets, and the apartment must be smoke-free.

cases.essential_rule: KF1 is essential, and at least one of KF3 or KF4 is essential (both parts of the question must be answered).
cases.expected_behavior: Answers both what the rent includes and what is required of the tenant.

cases.input: What parts does the example job application consist of?

key_facts.fact: The application has an introduction, a main part and a conclusion (INLEDNING / HUVUDPARAGRAF / SLUTSATS, or INTRO / BODY / END).
The introduction names the position and where the advertisement was seen.
The main part describes experience and personal qualities.
The conclusion looks forward to talking more or to an interview and ends with a closing such as 'Med vänliga hälsningar'.

cases.expected_behavior: Describes the parts of the example job application.

cases.input: How is the book "Förbered dig för allmän språkexamen" meant to be used?

key_facts.fact: The exercises can be practised with a teacher in a guided course, with a friend, or on your own.
The book has seven sections based on CEFR theme areas.
It helps you practise speaking and writing for the intermediate-level language test.
You can ask a teacher or a friend who knows Swedish well for feedback on your writing tasks.

cases.expected_behavior: Explains how the book is meant to be used according to its own introduction.

cases.input: Generate five revision questions about the structure of the writing test.
cases.expected_behavior: Produces five revision questions answerable from the writing-test material (S01 KF1-KF5).

extra_rules.G_PASS: Exactly five questions; all answerable from the retrieved material; together they cover at least 3 of S01 KF1-KF5; no question asserts facts that are not in the material.
extra_rules.G_PARTIAL: 3-4 or 6 or more questions; or exactly one question not answerable from the material; or fewer than 3 of S01 KF1-KF5 covered.
extra_rules.G_FAIL: 2 or fewer questions; or most questions not answerable from the material; or questions not about the writing test.

cases.input: What could I write in Swedish if a package I paid extra for arrived late and damaged?

key_facts.fact: The complaint example describes a package that came both late and damaged ('inte bara sent men också defekt').
It mentions that extra was paid for fast delivery.
Say what you want: your money back or a new package.
Ask for compensation for at least the extra amount paid.

cases.essential_rule: KF3 is essential, and the answer must give Swedish wording (the question explicitly asks what to write in Swedish).
cases.expected_behavior: Gives Swedish complaint wording based on the late-and-damaged package example.

cases.input: Compare how the course notes and the example texts describe writing a review.

key_facts.fact: The course notes describe a review as context or description, good and bad points in a type-4 structure, and a recommendation.
The example texts show a positive review (Restaurang Glädje) and a negative review (Hotell Mörker), each with reasons.
The course notes give their own examples (a negative review of TechKöp and positive reviews of SuperPro headphones or a hotel).
Reviews end with a recommendation or a warning.

cases.essential_rule: KF1 and KF2 are essential: both sides of the comparison must be covered.
cases.expected_behavior: Compares the course-notes guidance on reviews with the example review texts.

cases.input: How long should it be?
cases.expected_behavior: Recognises that the question has no clear referent instead of pretending it is precise.

extra_rules.G_PASS: States that the question is unclear or asks what 'it' refers to; or gives the material's lengths per text type while explicitly saying it is assuming the writing tasks.
extra_rules.G_PARTIAL: Gives the per-text-type lengths from the material without acknowledging the ambiguity.
extra_rules.G_FAIL: Gives one unqualified length, or lengths that are not in the material.

cases.input: I am preparing for the Swedish language exam next month and I am quite nervous about the writing part, because in my home country we never had to write formal letters or opinion texts in the same way. I have read that there are different kinds of texts, some informal and some formal, and that the exam has a time limit, but I am not sure how many texts I actually have to write, how long each of them should be, and which kind of text is supposed to be the longest one. Could you explain how the writing part is organised, so that I can plan my time properly during the exam?

key_facts.fact: The writing part consists of three texts.
The writing part takes 55 minutes in total.
The informal and the formal text are each 50-80 words long.
The opinion text is 100-150 words long.
The opinion text is the longest text.

cases.essential_rule: KF1, KF3, KF4 and KF5 are essential: the question explicitly asks how many texts, how long each is, and which is longest.
cases.expected_behavior: Handles the long question and explains how the writing part is organised.

cases.input: Vilka delar ingår i den muntliga delen av provet?

key_facts.fact: Berätta is a part of the speaking test.
Dialog is a part of the speaking test.
Reagera / Situationer is a part of the speaking test.
Din åsikt is a part of the speaking test.
At least one correct timing for a speaking-test part is given.

cases.essential_rule: KF1-KF4 are essential: the question asks which parts the oral test includes. The answer may be in Swedish or English.
cases.expected_behavior: Answers the Swedish question with the parts of the speaking test.

cases.input: How much time do I have for the writing part of the exam, and what score do I need to pass it?

key_facts.fact: The writing part takes 55 minutes for three texts.
The required pass score is not given in the course material; the answer says so and does not invent a score.

cases.essential_rule: KF1 and KF2 are both essential (two explicit subquestions).
cases.expected_behavior: Answers the time question and states that the pass score is not covered.

cases.input: 我想投诉邻居太吵，用瑞典语可以怎么说？

key_facts.fact: 'gör oljud' (makes noise, e.g. at night).
'pratar högt' (talks loudly).
'lyssnar på musik för högt' / 'mitt i natten' (plays music too loud / in the middle of the night).
'hunden skäller' (the dog barks).

cases.essential_rule: The answer must give Swedish wording. The answer may be in any language.
cases.expected_behavior: Gives Swedish phrases for complaining about noisy neighbours, taken from the course material.

extra_rules.G_PARTIAL: Exactly 1 of KF1-KF4, or only correct Swedish phrases that are not from the material.
extra_rules.G_FAIL: No Swedish wording, a wrong or misleading translation, or a contradiction of the material.
